references.text: Both verses are part of the same confrontation and show Laban's inconsistent use of ownership over his daughters as a rhetorical tool.
Direct dialogue pair where Jacob's fear of losing his daughters (Gen 31:31) meets Laban's claim that he can do nothing for them (Gen 31:43).
Direct response in the same conflict; Laban's ownership claim (Gen 31:43) is met by Jacob's appeal to justice and innocence (Gen 31:36).
